name: Loose cotton clothing / washing sheets
lead: Wearing loose, breathable clothing such as cotton and laundering clothes and bedding regularly are habits people adopt to keep skin clear, particularly on the back, chest, shoulders and jawline where rubbing and trapped sweat can lead to breakouts. The aim is a cleaner, more even complexion with fewer friction-related pimples and less scarring or discolouration.

Wikipedia describes acne mechanica as acne caused by friction, heat and pressure on the skin from tight clothing, straps, sports gear or a phone held against the face, made worse by sweat and poor airflow [1]. It says athletes, soldiers in warm climates, teens and young adults are most affected, and that prevention includes loose, breathable clothing, cotton rather than polyester or rayon, and showering soon after exercise [1]. The same article notes the condition typically clears once friction and heat are avoided and can leave scarring or discolouration if rubbing continues [1].

Wikipedia's folliculitis article adds that clothing friction can injure hair follicles, which are then often infected by Staphylococcus bacteria [2]. On T Nation, lifters discussing back acne ('bacne') mention loose clothing, changing out of sweaty gym clothes and laundry habits [3][4][5].

paras: Practitioners choose loose cotton garments to limit rubbing and trapped sweat, and launder sheets and clothes frequently. Wikipedia lists tight clothing, straps, sports gear and phones held to the face as sources of friction in acne mechanica [1].

Acne mechanica is acne triggered by friction, heat and pressure, and Wikipedia says it can leave scarring or discolouration if rubbing continues [1]. Reducing the triggers is the way people try to prevent breakouts on areas such as the back, chest and shoulders, and clothing rubbing on follicles is described as a trigger of folliculitis [2]. People with acne-prone skin and men, who produce more skin oil, are described as more susceptible [1].

In a T Nation thread on back acne, a poster listed laundry habits: avoid fabric softener, limit detergent and wash very sweaty gym clothes soon rather than leaving them in a pile [3]. Another poster in a 2007 thread wrote that dermatologists advise avoiding tight-fitting clothing because sweat and congested pores worsen back acne [4]. A user on testosterone therapy wrote that his back acne was probably due more to not changing out of workout clothes [5]. Another thread discusses benzoyl peroxide cleansers for back acne [6].

No studies found on loose cotton clothing or washing sheets for acne. Wikipedia notes that the acne mechanica article is flagged as needing more reliable medical sources and says there is no direct cure beyond avoiding friction and heat and keeping skin clean [1].

lore.intro: Back-acne threads on T Nation mention clothing choice and laundry habits alongside topical products.

claims.claim: Tight clothing and sweaty gym clothes worsen back acne
claims.believers: Posters say excessive sweat and congested pores make back acne worse and recommend avoiding tight clothing and changing out of sweaty clothes [4][5].
claims.experts: Wikipedia attributes acne mechanica to friction, heat, pressure and sweat, and lists loose breathable fabrics and prompt showering as prevention [1].

claims.claim: Laundry products such as fabric softener can contribute to body acne
claims.believers: A poster advises avoiding fabric softener and limiting detergent for back acne [3].
claims.experts: No studies on laundry products and acne were found in the sources reviewed.

card.summary: Loose cotton and clean bedding to cut friction acne; suggested generally, untested.

quick.overview:
Some people wear loose cotton and wash sheets often to reduce acne from rubbing and trapped sweat.

General references suggest loose breathable fabric for acne mechanica; no trials were found.
quick.mechanism: Looser, breathable fabric reduces friction, heat and sweat retention on skin.

Fewer friction-related breakouts, clearer skin on body and jaw
angle.text: The habit targets the mechanical and sweat-related triggers of acne mechanica. Cotton and loose cuts reduce rubbing and heat, and changing out of sweaty clothes and washing fabrics is meant to keep pores clearer.
